terminal.description: A shell in your workspace: node run.mjs <file> runs a query file against a fresh copy of the bakehouse database.

tasks.title: Build the October delivery log
tasks.description:
A cafe says an October delivery never arrived. Odile needs the log with names, not ids.

In `queries/1-october-deliveries.sql`, return one row per **delivered** order whose `ordered_on` falls in October 2026 (`2026-10-01` to `2026-10-31`), with these columns:

- `order_id`: the order's id
- `cafe`: the cafe's name
- `driver`: the driver's name
- `ordered_on`

Sort by `ordered_on`, then by `order_id`. This needs three tables: `orders`, `cafes` and `drivers`.

The check compares rows and their order on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: Join orders to cafes and select the order id with the cafe name.
Add a second join to drivers.
Filter by status and date range, then sort.
Rename the columns to the names the task asks for.
hints: Each order row holds a cafe_id and a driver_id. Those are what you join on.
Both cafes and drivers have a column called name. Give each table a short alias and write c.name, d.name with AS to tell them apart.
Write JOIN cafes AS c ON c.id = o.cafe_id and JOIN drivers AS d ON d.id = o.driver_id, then WHERE on status and BETWEEN on the two dates.

tasks.title: Count orders for every driver
tasks.description:
Odile is planning rotas and wants to see how many orders each driver has been given, including any driver with none yet.

In `queries/2-driver-load.sql`, return one row for **every** driver with:

- `driver`: the driver's name
- `orders`: how many orders have that driver's id as `driver_id` (any status), `0` when there are none

Sort by `orders` from most to fewest, then by `driver` from A to Z.

The check compares rows and their order on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: Join drivers to orders and count per driver. Compare the driver count with `SELECT * FROM drivers;`.
Change the join so drivers without orders stay in the result.
Make sure a driver with no orders shows 0, not 1.
hints: An inner join drops a driver who has no matching order, so that driver never reaches the count.
LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table and fills the right side with NULL when nothing matches.
COUNT(*) counts that NULL-filled row as 1. Count a column from the orders side, such as o.id, which is NULL when there is no match.

tasks.title: Find products nobody orders
tasks.description:
Tobias suspects a few products are baked for nobody. Find them.

In `queries/3-never-ordered.sql`, return `name` and `category` for every product that does not appear in any row of `order_items`. Row order does not matter.

The check compares your rows with the expected rows on the shipped data and on a hidden dataset.
nextSteps: LEFT JOIN products to order_items and look at the rows with NULL on the right.
Select the two columns the task asks for.
hints: A product with orders matches one or more order_items rows. A product without orders matches none.
After a LEFT JOIN, the right side of an unmatched row is NULL in every column.
Filter with WHERE on a column from order_items that is never NULL in real rows, such as its product_id, being IS NULL.
